newsitem.title: USA: Nabisco inundated with chowder cracker fans' calls.
newsitem.headline: Nabisco inundated with chowder cracker fans' calls.

text.p: Food giant RJR Nabisco conceded Monday it was being inundated with "thousands of calls" from people around the country from people about the culinary downsizing of their favourite chowder cracker.

Nabisco officials have scheduled an announcement for Feb. 4 in Boston to respond to a campaign to save the Crown Pilot cracker, which the company stopped baking last May after 204 years of production.

Residents of Chebeague Island, which is located about 15 miles from Portland, rallied in defence of Crown Pilots and received national publicity for their plea for people to call Nabisco's consumer telephone hotline.
Since that publicity began, "We've gotten thousands of calls, e-mail, letters from around the country on this issue," Nabisco spokeswoman Ann Smith said, adding, "We are a responsive company."
While Smith would not say what decision has made on the Philadelphia-baked Crown Pilot's fate, she did note the news conference and the "loyalty" of the cracker's fans.
Crown Pilots were introduced in 1792 at a Newburyport, Mass., bakery, which became part of Nabisco -- the National Biscuit Company - in 1898. The cracker was Nabisco's oldest product line.
